title: P18 Session 2: API 653 Fitness-for-Service Assessment Integrating RAPWIN Ultrasonic Data with Claude
goal: My goal in Session 2 is to evaluate localized corrosion and conduct a Fitness-for-Service (FFS) assessment by integrating ultrasonic inspection data with Claude AI.
occupation: Metallurgical Engineer & Senior NDT / QA/QC Welding Inspector

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude interpreted the C scan images and correlated it with the API 653, 4.3.

Step 1.step_name: Raw NDT Data Loading and Visual C-Scan Mapping
Step 1.step_action: Load the ultrasonic C-Scan/B-Scan raw inspection files into RAPWIN software to establish the baseline nominal wall thickness and visual color scale. Perform an initial visual inspection of the scanned shell plate grid to locate critical thickness loss areas and potential sensor signal artifacts.

nodes.label: Browse pre-existing reference report in Google Docs
nodes.detail: The session opens on a Chrome tab already showing a Google Doc titled 'TK731_ShellCourse1_Final_Report_and_Inspection_Plan', with a populated tank datasheet table (Figure 1: TK-731, Ecopetrol S.A., riveted API 12B/API 650 9th Ed. Appendix E) and a document outline (Executive Summary through Scan Location Results). The participant narrates aloud that he wants to build a new report about API 653 in-service tank inspection and upload characteristics/images to Claude, using this earlier document purely as a mental reference for what a finished report should contain; the doc itself is only previewed, never edited.

nodes.label: Open new Claude chat and begin draft prompt
nodes.detail: The participant opens a new Claude.ai chat, attaches the tank datasheet screenshot, and begins typing an opening prompt about building an API 653 report for the first shell course, narrating his intent as he types.

nodes.label: Load C-Scan/B-Scan files into RAPWIN
nodes.detail: He switches to RAPWIN/Raptor NDT Software and opens scan files via the SD-card Open dialog, working through the Quantum settings dialog; files opened include 'tk701 15 anillo b.P30' and 'tk703 10a superior.P30'.

nodes.label: Isolate thickness bands on the C-scan color palette
nodes.detail: He repeatedly reconfigures the color thickness scale/palette on the C-scan grid to isolate specific thickness bands (0-10mm, 10-20mm, 20-29.46mm), taking a screenshot of each isolated band to capture the visual corrosion pattern.

nodes.label: Attach color-coded C-scan screenshots to the Claude draft
nodes.detail: He returns to the Claude tab and attaches the color-coded C-scan band screenshots to the still-unsent draft message, typing that the max thickness found is 29.46mm and that all image dimensions are in millimeters.

Step 2.step_name: Quantitative Feature Extraction and Defect Bounding
Step 2.step_action: Extract the exact minimum remaining thickness (t min) and export the thickness distribution matrix from RAPWIN. Define the spatial boundaries (Lx X Ly) of the localized thin area (LTA) to quantify the physical extent of the corroded region.

nodes.label: Switch RAPWIN dataset to the correct tank (tk703)
nodes.detail: Continuing in RAPWIN, the participant remarks aloud at ~15:41 ('I had to change the information because it is another tank but no problem'), switching the loaded dataset to the tk703 file set and reopening B-scan/histogram views for that tank.

nodes.label: Recalibrate thickness color scale via Setup Scale dialog
nodes.detail: He uses the Setup Scale dialog (Range/Offset fields) to recalibrate the thickness color scale across bands from 0-10mm through 30-40mm, preparing the C-scan for precise readings on the tk703 data. Frame evidence confirms a genuine second visit: shortly after the single cursor reading recorded at 20:00 (s2n3), the Setup Scale dialog reopens (still visible at 20:03) and the participant cycles through progressively wider Range/Offset values (0-10, 10-20/30-2, up to a 40.28-wide band anchored on the just-read max thickness) continuously until roughly 23:33, when the window switches to RAPWIN's Histogram tool.

nodes.label: Finish building the Claude draft message with new readings
nodes.detail: He returns to the still-unsent Claude draft, attaches the remaining C-scan screenshots (5-6 total across Steps 1-2), and revises the typed prompt text to state the new max thickness (~40mm), the four thickness bands (0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30-40mm), that the report covers the first shell course, and that the material specification is unknown so Claude should determine max L and max fill.

nodes.label: Re-read the completed prompt before sending
nodes.detail: With the screenshots attached and the request written, the participant reads through the drafted prompt in the Claude input box before submitting it.

Step 3.step_name: API 653 Code Compliance & Vintage Steel Analysis via Claude
Step 3.step_action: Prompt Claude to apply API 653 4.3.2.1 critical length formulas and 4.3.3 localized thinning acceptance limits using the RAPWIN dataset. Ask Claude to evaluate if the indications could correspond to manufacturing steel defects based on the tank's construction era, or if material should be treated as 'unknown'.

nodes.label: Send the prompt to Claude
nodes.detail: The participant submits the completed prompt, with the ten attached C-scan/B-scan/histogram screenshots, asking Claude for an API 653 Section 4.3 report including the maximum L and maximum fill height.

nodes.label: Research §4.3 requirements, build the evaluation report, and flag key results
nodes.detail: Claude states it will research the exact API 653 §4.3 requirements before calculating rather than guessing at the code text, then thinks for ~2 minutes while searching the web and fetching the energy-steel.com API 653 PDF, confirming the §4.3 fifth-edition text including riveted-tank provisions in §4.3.4 and the critical-length formula in §4.3.2. Claude then reads its docx-generation skill, checks an additional uploaded image, verifies the docx library, writes build_report.js, and generates the report — converting to PDF for visual spot-checks, finding the TOC field renders empty outside Word, removing it, and rebuilding to a clean 12-page document. Claude shares 'TK-731_Shell_Course1_API653_4.3_Evaluation.docx' and flags the key results: critical length L ≈ 712 mm and max fill ≈ 6.7–7.5 m (depending on whether the 10 mm reading is real corrosion), §4.3.4.1 default stress values used (S = 145 MPa, E = 1.0) since the riveted tank's material spec is unknown, and profile-averaged thickness t1 flagged as an unresolved Priority 1 open item.

nodes.label: Audit report Sections 1-2 against the code
nodes.detail: The participant reads through Section 1 (Purpose/Scope) and Section 2 (Tank ID data, including fields marked 'N.E.'/not established) in the DOCX preview, cross-checking the transcribed values against the API 653 standard he calls 'the red book'.

nodes.label: Audit report Sections 3-4 (code basis and inspection method)
nodes.detail: He reviews Section 3 (Applicable Code Basis for riveted API 12B construction, using S=145MPa, E=1.0 defaults) and Section 4 (UTCM inspection method), checking that Claude's stated assumptions match the code's default provisions for unknown material.

nodes.label: Audit corrosion-mapping results and calculations
nodes.detail: He reviews Section 5 (corrosion-mapping histogram results, dominant peak ~27-28mm) and Section 7 calculations — minimum acceptable thickness t-min for G=0.90 vs G=1.00 giving 16.0mm/17.8mm, the corroded-area acceptance check against 60% of t-min, critical length L calculated at approximately 712mm against a 720mm API-653 allowable maximum, and max-fill height results of roughly 6.7-7.5m.

nodes.label: Re-check originally attached C-scan images against the report
nodes.detail: He scrolls back up in the chat to re-look at the originally attached C-scan screenshots and the original prompt text, verifying Claude's interpretation of dimensions, materials, and inspection items against the code before moving on.

Step 4.step_action: Synthesize RAPWIN graphical outputs with Claude's refined API 653 structural compliance text into a final inspection report. Formulate clear, actionable engineering recommendations (e.g., Pass/Fail rating, patch repair design, or required re-inspection intervals). Note: a documented 'Spatial Cross-Verification in RAPWIN' (overlaying Claude's calculated critical length/acceptance boundaries onto the C-scan) is described in the source workflow document for this step, but a denser re-verification pass over this window (~75 frames at 15-20s intervals) found no on-screen evidence this occurred; it is represented honestly below as it actually happened.

nodes.label: Incidental alt-tab to RAPWIN (not a spatial cross-verification)
nodes.detail: At approximately 52:45-52:52 the participant briefly switches away from the Claude tab to the already-open 'tk703 10a.P30 - Raptor' window (the same session from Steps 1-2), opens the File menu (Open/Save As/Export/Print, and a recent-files list: tk703 10a.P30, C:\SCAN, tk703 10a superior.P30, tk703 lam23b.P30), then closes the menu without selecting anything. The Data/Value panel is completely empty, no cursor coordinate is read, no Setup Scale dialog is touched, and no overlay, marker, or boundary line is drawn on the C-scan — this is an incidental alt-tab or muscle-memory click on the still-open taskbar item, not the deliberate RAPWIN spatial cross-verification of Claude's critical-length/acceptance boundaries that the workflow document describes for this step.

nodes.label: Re-check attached images and download the report
nodes.detail: He returns to the Claude chat, scrolls once more to the originally-attached prompt and C-scan images, then downloads the finished DOCX report (~53:00-53:10).

nodes.label: Check the downloaded report in Downloads, then browse the original C-scan screenshots
nodes.detail: After downloading the report, the participant opens File Explorer to the Downloads folder, then switches to the Pictures/Screenshots folder and opens the original C-scan screenshots used in the prompt.

nodes.label: Re-read the report from the beginning
nodes.detail: He returns to the Claude DOCX preview and scrolls it from the very beginning again — Section 1 Purpose and Scope, Section 2 Tank Identification Data, Section 3 Applicable Code Basis — consistent with narration about starting over at 'page one' to assemble/verify the final report. The recording ends at 56:26 with this review still in progress; no Google Docs editing, PDF export, or completed final report was observed within the captured session.

Step 1.step_name: Raw NDT Data Loading and Visual C-Scan Mapping
Step 1.step_action: Load the ultrasonic C-Scan/B-Scan raw inspection files into RAPWIN software to establish the baseline nominal wall thickness and visual color scale. Perform an initial visual inspection of the scanned shell plate grid to locate critical thickness loss areas and potential sensor signal artifacts.
Step 1.input: Ultrasonic raw scan file  and tank baseline design specifications (nominal thickness, diameter).
Step 1.output: Configured C-Scan visual map in RAPWIN highlighting localized thinning zones with defined thickness ranges.
rubrics: Accurate configuration of RAPWIN thickness color-palette matching the nominal and minimum expected wall thickness
Clear visual identification and localization of thinning areas vs. potential acoustic signal artifacts.

ratings.output_quality_reason: The agent accurately configured the C-scan visual map parameters in RAPWIN based on the survey data. It established the baseline nominal shell thickness  and clearly differentiated genuine wall thinning zones along the lower panel from acoustic signal artifacts

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent effectively loaded and interpreted the UTCM C-scan, B-scan, and histogram dataset like an NDT inspector, establishing baseline parameters and isolating critical indications.

Step 2.step_name: Quantitative Feature Extraction and Defect Bounding
Step 2.step_action: Extract the exact minimum remaining thickness (t min) and export the thickness distribution matrix from RAPWIN. Define the spatial boundaries (Lx X Ly) of the localized thin area (LTA) to quantify the physical extent of the corroded region.
Step 2.input: Processed RAPWIN C-Scan map and thickness histogram data.
Step 2.output: Summary table of t min  values, spatial coordinates (Lx, Ly), and exported thickness distribution grid .
rubrics: Precise measurement and extraction of t min and the critical defect boundaries (Lx X Ly)
Successful export of a clean, structured thickness matrix suitable for external AI processing.

ratings.output_quality_reason:
rom 1-5 (1 not satisfy, 5 satisfy): 5
Reason for your rating:  The output directly addresses all required actions in Step 2. It accurately extracts the minimum thickness. Additionally, it organizes the thickness distribution histogram into structured bands and specifies the exact spatial grid resolution for downstream processing.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent successfully parsed the RAPWIN UTCM C-scan, histogram, and project evaluation document to extract required quantitative parameters, perform API 653 critical length calculations, and format the outputs into clean tables ready for further computational analysis.

Step 3.step_name: API 653 Code Compliance & Vintage Steel Analysis via Claude
Step 3.step_action: Prompt Claude to apply API 653 4.3.2.1 critical length formulas and 4.3.3 localized thinning acceptance limits using the RAPWIN dataset. Ask Claude to evaluate if the indications could correspond to manufacturing steel defects based on the tank's construction era, or if material should be treated as 'unknown'.
Step 3.input: Exported RAPWIN thickness matrix, t min, tank construction year, shell diameter, and fluid characteristics.
Step 3.output: Detailed API 653 structural integrity assessment draft and metallurgical defect profiling provided by Claude.
rubrics: Correct mathematical application of API 653 §4.3.2.1 critical length L and allowable stress equations
Rigorous evaluation of missing inputs (e.g., handling unknown material specifications and vintage steel manufacturing defects).

ratings.output_quality_reason: the output executed the required mathematical formulations under API 653, 4.3.2.1 and 4.3.4.1 it also detail vintage steel manufacturing anomalies.

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent combined the RAPWIN inspection dataset with API 653 formulas and metallurgical principles, producing a structural integrity draft and defect profiling assessment;

Correct identification of coverage limitations (e.g., necessity of expanding scan coverage if corrosion extends off-grid).

ratings.output_quality_reason: the cross verification precisely aligned the calculated critical length and it correctly identifies that the localized thinning extends to the lower scans boundary near the bottom cheam zone.

Step 5.output: Completed API 653 Fitness-for-Service evaluation report ready for client submission.
